mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate tighter credit conditions, prompting a flight to quality and reducing equity risk premia, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar rising-rate regimes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10), or the effect size is smaller than the 95% confidence interval of the historical mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index by at least 0.5% over two months signals disinflation, prompting central banks to pause rate hikes and reducing real risk-free rates, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: In disinflationary regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior month's average (p > 0.10), or the inflation decline is not sustained past 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 50,000 jobs in the prior month predicts a temporary boost in consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of weak demand, similar labor growth does not produce positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the RSAFS (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds the prior month by at least 3% and coincides with rising HOUST (housing starts), it signals resilient consumer and housing market momentum, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by ≥3% and HOUST increases in the prior month
failure_condition: In similar high-growth months, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) contraction of more than 2% followed by a rebound of at least 1% in the next month indicates a supply-side shock, which temporarily elevates volatility and compresses option values, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in month t, then rebounds in month t+1
failure_condition: During comparable supply shocks, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tightening labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and equity risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In tight-labor regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for two consecutive months in a non-recessionary macro context, it signals persistent policy accommodation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months and macro context is non-recessionary
failure_condition: In similar high-accommodation regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 (GDP demand) and HOUST (housing starts) by at least 5% in the prior month creates a dual-demand signal that amplifies optimism about economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥5% and HOUST increases by ≥5% in the prior month
regime_hint: Dual demand and housing cycle acceleration
failure_condition: In months with only one of the two signals rising, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).
